package.name: openssh
package.description: the OpenBSD SSH implementation (Werewolf: no PAM, SELinux, zlib or PKCS#11)

pipeline.name: Fetch the locked source commit
pipeline.runs:
git init -q .
for delay in 0 15 45; do
  sleep "$delay"
  for source in https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable.git; do
    if git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c fetch.fsckObjects=true fetch --no-tags --depth=1 "$source" a8c72b842423f0774f542d3c2197247c3dd28d74; then
      test "$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)" = a8c72b842423f0774f542d3c2197247c3dd28d74
      git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout -q --detach a8c72b842423f0774f542d3c2197247c3dd28d74
      exit 0
    fi
  done
done
echo "a8c72b842423f0774f542d3c2197247c3dd28d74: every source failed, three times" >&2
exit 1

pipeline.name: Apply Werewolf policy patches
pipeline.runs:
while IFS= read -r name; do
  patch -p1 --forward --batch --fuzz=2 --no-backup-if-mismatch -i "patches/$name" || exit 1
done < patches/series

set -euo pipefail
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /tmp/testkey -N '' -q
test -f /tmp/testkey && test -f /tmp/testkey.pub
ssh-keygen -l -f /tmp/testkey.pub | grep -F SHA256

scriptlets.post-install:
#!/bin/sh
if grep -q '^openssl-config-fipshardened-3.1.2' /etc/apk/world; then
   ssh-keygen -q -N "" -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key -t rsa
   ssh-keygen -q -N "" -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key -t ecdsa
else
   ssh-keygen -A -q -N ""
fi

pipeline.runs:
ssh-keygen -A -q -N ""    # This is unfortunate, but scriplets don't run in test environments, so force this here
/usr/bin/sshd

mkdir -p "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/usr
mv "${{targets.destdir}}"/usr/bin "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/usr/

mkdir -p "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/etc/ssh
mv "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/ssh/moduli "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/etc/ssh/
mv "${{targets.destdir}}"/etc/ssh/ssh_config "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/etc/ssh/
mkdir -p "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d
sed -i 's|\(^# Host\)|Include /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/*.conf\n\n\1|' "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/etc/ssh/ssh_config

set -euo pipefail
conf="/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/_wolfi.conf"
trap "rm -f $conf" EXIT
echo "Tag YouAreIt" > "$conf"
ssh -G _ | grep -i '^Tag YouAreIt$'

mkdir -p "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/usr/lib/systemd/system
mkdir -p ${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/
install -Dm644  sshd.service "${{targets.subpkgdir}}"/usr/lib/systemd/system
echo "enable sshd.service" > "${{targets.subpkgdir}}/usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/80-sshd.preset"

set -euo pipefail
conf="/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/_wolfi.conf"
trap "rm -f $conf" EXIT
echo "Banner /does-not-exist" > "$conf"
ssh-keygen -A -q -N ""
sshd -T | grep -Fi 'Banner /does-not-exist'

ssh-keygen -A -q -N ""    # This is unfortunate, but scriplets don't run in test environments, so force this here
/usr/bin/sshd

pipeline.name: Programs link no PAM, SELinux or zlib, and refuse compression and PKCS#11
pipeline.runs:
cat > /tmp/openssh-probe.sh <<'WEREWOLF_OPENSSH_PROBE'
# The installed packages hold Werewolf's OpenSSH build policy.
set -eu

loader=
for path in /usr/lib/ld-linux-*.so.* /lib/ld-linux-*.so.* /lib64/ld-linux-*.so.*; do
	if [ -x "$path" ]; then
		loader=$path
		break
	fi
done
test -n "$loader"

# No program loads PAM, SELinux (with its PCRE2) or zlib. Each keeps libcrypto,
# whose ECDSA verifies P-256 security keys.
for program in /usr/bin/sshd /usr/lib/ssh/sshd-session /usr/lib/ssh/sshd-auth \
	/usr/bin/ssh /usr/bin/ssh-agent /usr/bin/ssh-keygen; do
	libraries=$("$loader" --list "$program")
	for library in libpam.so libselinux.so libpcre2 libz.so; do
		if printf '%s\n' "$libraries" | grep -q "$library"; then
			echo "$program loads $library" >&2
			exit 1
		fi
	done
	printf '%s\n' "$libraries" | grep -q libcrypto.so
done

work=$(mktemp -d)
ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f "$work/host"
sshd -T -f /dev/null -h "$work/host" > "$work/defaults"
grep -qx 'Compression no' "$work/defaults"
if grep -qi '^UsePAM' "$work/defaults"; then
	echo 'sshd has PAM support' >&2
	exit 1
fi
if sshd -T -f /dev/null -h "$work/host" -o Compression=yes > /dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo 'sshd accepts Compression yes' >&2
	exit 1
fi
test "$(ssh -Q compression)" = none

# Both security key types, ed25519 and P-256 (Apple's Secure Enclave), remain.
keys=sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com,sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com
sshd -T -f /dev/null -h "$work/host" -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=$keys |
	grep -qx "PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms $keys"
ssh -Q key | grep -qx sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com

# The client takes no PKCS#11 provider.
ssh -G -I /nonexistent localhost 2>&1 > /dev/null | grep -qx 'no support for PKCS#11.'
rm -rf "$work"
WEREWOLF_OPENSSH_PROBE
sh /tmp/openssh-probe.sh
